claims.text: The driver did not give the notice POL-RD-21 requires before or at the point of deviation. The chat log carries exactly two messages, both sent before the trip began (20:38:52 and 20:39:12) and both about the pickup point — 'At Dempsey Block 8 drop off' and 'ok' — and the trip record's own POL-RD-21 field, derived.v7.messages_during_trip, is an empty list, with in_app_calls also empty. The deviation was detected at 20:54:05, some fourteen minutes after the trip started, so nothing was sent 'before or at the point of deviation' and the notification duty is unmet.

The driver's case rests on a bare verbal notice — his own filing asks 'Telling verbally also counts right?'. POL-RD-21 allows verbal notice only 'with the trip call recording as evidence', and the record contains no call recording: in_app_calls is empty on the trip record, and the clause's own note records that the records carry no call recordings at all. A verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established, and the clause's confirmation test — whether the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment — is not met, so this is not an agreed deviation and the rider's on-file account that he was told nothing is left standing.

The deviation is over tolerance, which closes the only rows that would leave the 0.86 SGD with the driver. POL-RD-22 measures the deviation from the platform's recorded distances — 13.2 km actual minus 12.0 km recommended = 1.20 km — against a 1.0 km tolerance, and 1.20 km exceeds it. Rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 (within tolerance, no refund) therefore cannot apply, and the driver cannot get the money back on a tolerance argument.

Traffic justification is not established either. POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window; the only advisory in the record, EV-ADVIS-05017-01, reports its own intersects_route field as undetermined — 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route' — and leaves justifies_reroute to the Judge. An advisory whose overlap with the recommended route is not shown cannot satisfy the intersect requirement of POL-RD-23, so the reroute is not made out as traffic-justified and row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies.

Even on the driver's most favourable account — that an accident on the CTE made the Braddell Road exit reasonable — the highest row he can reach is row (b), not row (a). Under POL-RD-24(a) a traffic-justified deviation escapes refund only if the rider was informed and agreed, and POL-RD-21 supplies the only proof of agreement: confirmation in the chat log or in a call recording. Neither exists. The agreed-deviation route to no refund is shut on this record, and the refund in row (b) is due.

It makes no difference to the rider which of the two open rows applies, because both pay the same sum and pay it to the rider. POL-RD-24 computes the refund as deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge — 1.20 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.86 SGD — and EV-FARE-05017 records exactly that: excess_distance_fare_sgd 0.86, refund_issued_sgd 0.86, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED. So whether the case is row (b) or row (d), the 0.86 SGD is the rider's, and nothing in POL-RD-24 moves any part of it back to the driver.

The case is ruleable now, and escalation would leave the driver in no better position. The deviation is 1.20 km, inside POL-RD-25's 2.0 km AI limit; the contested value is 0.86 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag (fraud_flags 0 on both); no safety indicator appears; and every artifact cited is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02's confidence cap does not bite. The single undetermined item — whether the advisory intersects the recommended route — cannot change the result, because rows (b) and (d) both refund the excess distance fare; there is no open question that needs a human to resolve.

The filing party is the driver, and the present state already takes the 0.86 SGD off his earnings and leaves it with the rider (fare_adjusted at 2026-09-10T03:30:02). POL-GEN-03 reads the outcome from the filer's claim against that state: because the driver's claim is not supported on this record, no sum is owed to him and the outcome is NO_ACTION — the present state stands, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both null.

The reroute was not an opportunistic detour: it was a response to a real-time traffic incident, which POL-RD-21 permits. The LTA record EV-ADVIS-05017-01 carries an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE), direction towards SLE, located 'after Braddell Road exit', valid 2026-09-09T20:23:22 to 2026-09-09T21:40:02 — a window that covers the recorded route_deviation_detected event at 20:54:05 and the whole trip window (20:40:02 to 21:04:02). The CTE is one of the roads the trip record lists on the recommended route (trip_record.optimal_route_via), and the recorded deviation point is the PIE / CTE interchange at the Braddell Road exit, the very point the advisory's location field names. ACCIDENT falls within POL-RD-23's admissible 'incident' types, so the traffic-justification requirement is met on the record's own fields, not on general geography.

ruling.explanation: To the driver and the rider: The trip record shows actual distance 13.2 km against a recommended 12.0 km, so the deviation is 1.20 km, over the 1.0 km tolerance. The LTA advisory (ACCIDENT on CTE towards SLE after Braddell Road exit, valid 20:23-21:40) covers the trip window and the CTE segment of the recommended route, so I accept the driver's point that the reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. However, the question whether the driver notified the rider cannot be established. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat or verbally with a call recording; the chat log has only two pre-trip messages about the pickup point, and the trip record's in_app_calls is empty. The driver's verbal notice has no recording, and POL-RD-21 provides that such notice cannot be established. Since POL-GEN-26 names 'whether the driver notified the rider' as a fact that must be established, and POL-RD-24 has no row for a traffic-justified deviation over 1 km where notification is unestablished, the case must go to a human reviewer. I therefore reject the rider's argument that row (b) applies: the record does not establish that the rider was not informed, only that notification cannot be established. The 0.86 SGD already refunded (1.20 km x 0.72 SGD/km) is held pending review. No safety or fraud flags apply, and no route-deviation referral clause exists.

How this was decided, for both of you.

Distance (POL-RD-22). The recommended route was 12.0 km and the car drove 13.2 km — a deviation of 1.20 km, taken from the platform's own recorded distances on the trip record, not re-measured from the trace. That is over the 1.0 km tolerance, so the 'within tolerance, no refund' rows cannot apply.

Was the reroute justified by traffic (POL-RD-23)? The LTA advisory for that evening records an accident on the Central Expressway (towards SLE) after the Braddell Road exit, valid 20:23 to 21:40, which covers the trip window (20:40 to 21:04). The CTE is part of the recommended route, and the driver left it exactly at the Braddell Road exit. On its road, direction and location the advisory does intersect the recommended route, and ACCIDENT is an admissible incident type, so the driver had a real reason to avoid that stretch.

That alone does not keep the money. POL-RD-21 requires a driver who reroutes to tell the rider before or at the point of deviation, by in-app chat or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence. Here there is no chat about the deviation — the only two messages (20:38:52 and 20:39:12) concern the pickup bay and predate the 20:40:02 trip start, and the trip record's own field for messages during the trip is empty — and there is no call recording (the in-app call list is empty). The driver says he told the rider verbally and the rider denies it; the policy provides that a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established, so the deviation is not an agreed one.

That places the case in POL-RD-24(b): traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — a refund of the excess distance fare. (If the advisory were instead read as not shown to intersect, row (d) gives the same refund, so the result does not turn on that point.) The excess distance fare is the deviation (1.20 km) times the per-km rate without surge (0.72 SGD) = 0.86 SGD — exactly what was refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (fare_adjusted, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 0.86).

The driver's escalation arguments do not hold. POL-RD-25's own limits are met: the deviation (1.20 km) is inside its 2.0 km AI cap and the disputed value (0.86 SGD) is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line, so an AI ruling is permitted on any confidence. Nor is POL-GEN-26 triggered: the facts the refund depends on — the deviation distance and the absence of any compliant notice in the chat log and trip record — are carried by complete artifacts at weight 1.0, so nothing needed for the outcome is missing or impaired, and the confidence cap is 1.0 (well above the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires).

Because the driver filed and his claim to take back the 0.86 SGD is not supported, while the rider is owed that refund under POL-RD-24, the present state stands: no action, and no further sum is moved in either direction. A route deviation carries no referral clause in this version, so none is added.

The driver filed to get that sum back. His claim is not supported, and the present state stands.

The deviation. The platform's recommended route was 12.0 km and the driver's actual route was 13.2 km (EV-TRIP-05017), a deviation of 1.20 km measured under POL-RD-22 (13.2 minus 12.0). That is more than the 1.0 km tolerance and less than POL-RD-25's 2.0 km AI limit, so the case is properly decided by the AI.

Whether the reroute was justified (POL-RD-23). The LTA record EV-ADVIS-05017-01 shows an accident on the CTE (towards SLE) after the Braddell Road exit, valid 20:23 to 21:40, covering the moment the driver left the recommended route at 20:54:05 (EV-TRIP-05017). The CTE is on the recommended route and the location matches the point of departure, so the driver's reason for the reroute is borne out. This does not change the result, for the reason below.

Whether the rider was told (POL-RD-21). A driver may reroute for real traffic only if he informs the rider before or at the point of deviation, by in-app chat or by a verbal notice supported by a call recording, and the deviation counts as agreed only where the chat log or a recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05017) holds two messages, both sent before the trip started and both about the pickup point ('At Dempsey Block 8 drop off' / 'ok'); the trip record's in-app call list is empty; and the record carries no call recording (POL-RD-21, note C11). The driver's account that he told the rider verbally, which the rider denies, cannot fill that gap: POL-RD-21 provides that a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established. The rider was therefore not informed, and the deviation was not an agreed one.

Which row applies (POL-RD-24). With the deviation over the 1.0 km tolerance and the rider not informed, the case falls in row (b) of POL-RD-24 — and, if the traffic justification were set aside, row (d) — and both rows refund the excess distance fare. Only row (a) (traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed) would leave the money with the driver, and it is not made out. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge: 1.20 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.86 SGD (POL-RD-24; EV-FARE-05017), exactly the sum already refunded (refund_issued_sgd 0.86, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED). This also disposes of the point that the advisory's overlap with the recommended route is left open: whether the reroute sits in row (b) or row (d), the refund is the same 0.86 SGD.

ledger.claim: The driver did not give the notice POL-RD-21 requires before or at the point of deviation. The chat log carries exactly two messages, both sent before the trip began (20:38:52 and 20:39:12) and both about the pickup point — 'At Dempsey Block 8 drop off' and 'ok' — and the trip record's own POL-RD-21 field, derived.v7.messages_during_trip, is an empty list, with in_app_calls also empty. The deviation was detected at 20:54:05, some fourteen minutes after the trip started, so nothing was sent 'before or at the point of deviation' and the notification duty is unmet.

The driver's case rests on a bare verbal notice — his own filing asks 'Telling verbally also counts right?'. POL-RD-21 allows verbal notice only 'with the trip call recording as evidence', and the record contains no call recording: in_app_calls is empty on the trip record, and the clause's own note records that the records carry no call recordings at all. A verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established, and the clause's confirmation test — whether the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment — is not met, so this is not an agreed deviation and the rider's on-file account that he was told nothing is left standing.

The deviation is over tolerance, which closes the only rows that would leave the 0.86 SGD with the driver. POL-RD-22 measures the deviation from the platform's recorded distances — 13.2 km actual minus 12.0 km recommended = 1.20 km — against a 1.0 km tolerance, and 1.20 km exceeds it. Rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 (within tolerance, no refund) therefore cannot apply, and the driver cannot get the money back on a tolerance argument.

Traffic justification is not established either. POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window; the only advisory in the record, EV-ADVIS-05017-01, reports its own intersects_route field as undetermined — 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route' — and leaves justifies_reroute to the Judge. An advisory whose overlap with the recommended route is not shown cannot satisfy the intersect requirement of POL-RD-23, so the reroute is not made out as traffic-justified and row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies.

Even on the driver's most favourable account — that an accident on the CTE made the Braddell Road exit reasonable — the highest row he can reach is row (b), not row (a). Under POL-RD-24(a) a traffic-justified deviation escapes refund only if the rider was informed and agreed, and POL-RD-21 supplies the only proof of agreement: confirmation in the chat log or in a call recording. Neither exists. The agreed-deviation route to no refund is shut on this record, and the refund in row (b) is due.

It makes no difference to the rider which of the two open rows applies, because both pay the same sum and pay it to the rider. POL-RD-24 computes the refund as deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge — 1.20 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.86 SGD — and EV-FARE-05017 records exactly that: excess_distance_fare_sgd 0.86, refund_issued_sgd 0.86, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED. So whether the case is row (b) or row (d), the 0.86 SGD is the rider's, and nothing in POL-RD-24 moves any part of it back to the driver.

The case is ruleable now, and escalation would leave the driver in no better position. The deviation is 1.20 km, inside POL-RD-25's 2.0 km AI limit; the contested value is 0.86 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag (fraud_flags 0 on both); no safety indicator appears; and every artifact cited is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02's confidence cap does not bite.
